The cypliers reprefeent to many holes lined into every line and paper, half an inch slunder > wherein pegs if different shapes are to feet, to reprend the federal forts of notes and characters of the tunes, which pegs the blind perform may know by feeling, as well as he does his keys of the organ or harphdon’s. To this, by keeping his fingers on the 2 lines, he feels the ferrugpas as they come on, and see for, to reprend the femoral loss of notes, on both line and faces; whilst his right hand flicks the respective key, kc. for left knowing the names of all his keys, hit lines, figures, and the mark of every peg. Let each peg be about half an inch high, when it is very fair. (N. B). The blind perken mault fril be taught the names of the above and places in both the treble and bals cliffs; and that he multi fed his treble and his system hand, and has had with the left hand; each being courtesy, as you may fee by the letters of the above table, A and B; and the learnt past spignants.
